scope: Qualitative project synthesis; no statistical ranking or new numerical fit.

boundary.label: Andrews-Hanna et al., 2008
boundary.consulted_material: Abstract: reconstruction of the boundary beneath Tharsis.

crust.label: Kim et al., 2023
crust.consulted_material: Abstract and seismic density constraints; no reanalysis of the data.

tides.label: Berne et al., 2026
tides.consulted_material: Tidal tomography sections and discussion of mechanisms.

south.label: Cheng et al., 2024
south.consulted_material: Abstract and description of the impact–interior evolution models.

feedback.label: Bonnet Gibet et al., 2022
feedback.consulted_material: Abstract: feedback between crustal thickness, heating and melting.

field.label: Langlais et al., 2019
field.consulted_material: Magnetic model already documented in the project data.

reversals.label: Steele et al., 2024
reversals.consulted_material: Abstract and cancellation mechanism during field reversals.

zircons.label: Bouvier et al., 2018
zircons.consulted_material: Abstract: seven zircons and isotopic interpretation of the reservoir.

alh.label: Steele et al., 2023
alh.consulted_material: Abstract and introduction; crystallization age cited from Lapen et al. (2010).

lafayette.label: Tremblay et al., 2024
lafayette.consulted_material: Abstract and age discussion; shock and ejection context cited by the authors.

ejection.label: Lagain et al., 2022
ejection.consulted_material: Abstract and introduction; source crater attribution proposed by the authors.

compatible.label: Conditionally compatible
compatible.meaning: A published mechanism can account for this aspect. This does not validate the entire family.

tension.label: Conditional tension
tension.meaning: A specific variant faces a difficulty; coupled variants still need examination.

not_tested.label: No comparable test
not_tested.meaning: The selected reading does not establish a common comparison. This is neither agreement nor rejection.

non_discriminating.label: Not decisive alone
non_discriminating.meaning: This observation can constrain several scenarios without selecting an origin on its own.

hypotheses.label: Northern impact
hypotheses.description: A large impact removes or thins the northern crust. Its geometry must remain recognizable after subsequent evolution.

hypotheses.label: Southern impact
hypotheses.description: Impact-induced melting can produce a thick southern crust. The cited models already include interior evolution.

hypotheses.label: Internal evolution
hypotheses.description: Convection, melting and heating can create or amplify an asymmetry. The cited feedback model mainly tests amplification.

hypotheses.label: Hybrid scenario
hypotheses.description: An impact creates an initial contrast, which heat redistribution and crustal growth can modify. This family overlaps with southern-impact scenarios.

observations.label: The shape of the north–south boundary
observations.observation: The boundary reconstructed beneath Tharsis is approximately elliptical, measuring 10,600 × 8,500 km.
observations.uncertainty: Removing the contribution of Tharsis is model-dependent. An ellipse is not an age measurement.

north.requirement: Preserve a basin boundary after subsequent modification.
north.next_test: Compare reconstructed boundaries using the same Tharsis correction.

south.summary: The boundary must also be reproduced.
south.requirement: Produce the topographic contrast and its shape within the same model.
south.next_test: Extract the final boundary from simulations and apply the same geometric criterion.

internal.summary: Amplification alone does not determine the shape.
internal.requirement: Asymmetric growth must explain the spatial geometry.
internal.next_test: Move from a two-hemisphere model to a predicted boundary.

hybrid.summary: Evolution can modify the initial boundary.
hybrid.requirement: Retain compatible geometry after mantle evolution.
hybrid.next_test: Measure boundary deformation between the impact and the final state.

observations.label: Crustal thickness and density
observations.observation: Seismic constraints favour similar crustal densities in the two hemispheres; a thickness difference remains necessary.
observations.uncertainty: Kim et al. exclude density contrasts above 200 kg/m³ in most of their models. Similar does not mean identical.

north.summary: Excavation must respect the final density.
north.requirement: Explain thickness, density and reworking together.
north.next_test: Apply the same density constraints to impact-model outputs.

south.summary: Melting can thicken the southern crust.
south.requirement: Simulated crustal production still needs a density check.
south.next_test: Compare simulated crusts with the same seismic inversion.

internal.requirement: The published feedback amplifies an initial contrast; its origin is a separate question.
internal.next_test: Test amplitude, composition and duration under the same thermal parameters.

hybrid.summary: An initial contrast can be amplified.
hybrid.requirement: Combine crust creation and evolution while conserving mass.
hybrid.next_test: Compare the final state under the same density assumptions.

observations.label: A warmer southern mantle?
observations.observation: Tidal tomography is interpreted as a present-day thermal contrast, with the south approximately 200–400 °C warmer.
observations.epoch: Present day; not the temperature of the primordial crust
observations.uncertainty: Composition and partial melting can change the conversion to temperature.

north.summary: Ancient impact heat alone is insufficient.
north.requirement: The tension concerns residual heat alone, not an impact followed by insulation.
north.next_test: Evaluate contrast duration after cooling and crustal growth.

south.summary: The final temperature still needs comparison.
south.requirement: An impact-and-evolution simulation must predict the present anomaly.
south.next_test: Compare thermal outputs with the tidal signal rather than an imposed temperature.

internal.requirement: Produce a lasting contrast compatible with interior structure.
internal.next_test: Also explore composition and partial melting.

hybrid.requirement: The initial contrast can evolve beneath unevenly insulating crust.
hybrid.next_test: Test crustal geometry and the present tidal response together.

observations.label: An uneven magnetic signal
observations.observation: The orbital crustal field shows strong regional and hemispheric contrasts.
observations.uncertainty: Depth, minerals, heating and polarity reversals affect the signal. A weakly magnetic basin does not prove the dynamo had stopped.

north.summary: The field also depends on recording.
north.requirement: Connect rock formation with acquisition and survival of magnetization.
north.next_test: Test mineral, cooling and field histories under common constraints.

south.summary: The field also depends on recording.

south.next_test: Test mineral, cooling and field histories under common constraints.

observations.label: Very ancient materials have survived
observations.observation: Zircons in NWA 7034 record crystallization around 4.43–4.48 billion years ago.
observations.kind: Grain dating followed by geological interpretation
observations.epoch: Local material history; see the chronology
observations.uncertainty: Grain survival does not directly date a planetary boundary. The extent of ancient crust remains to be established.
shared_inputs: Isotopic evolution model of the reservoir

north.summary: Every scenario must allow local survival.
north.requirement: Keep grain ages separate from the age of the dichotomy.
north.next_test: Predict the fraction and context of preserved ancient materials.

events.label: Extraction of the source reservoir

age.label: At least 4,547 Ma
age.uncertainty: Interpreted bound; no older limit specified here.

events.caveat: This source reservoir age is neither the grain age nor the age of the dichotomy.

events.label: Crystallization of seven zircons

age.label: 4,429.7–4,476.3 Ma
age.uncertainty: Range of ages across seven grains, not a confidence interval. Reported endpoint uncertainties: ±1.0 and ±0.9 Ma.

events.caveat: The grains did not all crystallize at the same time.

events.label: Rock crystallization

age.label: 4,091 ± 30 Ma
age.uncertainty: Reported ±30 Ma; confidence level not re-audited here.

events.method: Lapen et al. (2010) age cited by Steele et al.
events.caveat: Crystallization predates the magnetic reworking discussed.

events.label: Latest ancient recording discussed
events.caveat: Interpreted age marker, not direct dating of every grain or proof of a continuous dynamo.

events.label: Host-rock formation
events.method: Chronological context cited in Tremblay et al.
events.caveat: Rounded age marker, distinct from alteration.

events.label: Recorded shock episode
events.method: Thermochronology cited from Cassata et al. (2010)
events.caveat: Age discussed for Nakhla; linking it to the Lafayette shock remains an association.

events.label: Iddingsite formation
events.caveat: Dates the interpreted water–rock interaction; does not automatically date magnetization.

events.label: Ejection from Mars
events.method: Cosmic-ray exposure context cited from Cohen et al. (2017)
events.caveat: Ejection age marker for the nakhlite group, distinct from events within the rock.

events.label: Proposed ejection from Karratha

age.label: 5–10 Ma
age.uncertainty: Interpreted range; not an analytical 2σ interval.

events.method: Crater chronology and agreement with exposure ages
events.caveat: Proposed source attribution, not a directly observed location.

events.label: Formation of the dichotomy
events.caveat: No single age is inferred from the zircons or the present mantle.

events.label: Acquisition of magnetization
events.method: Mineral–magnetic component link still to be established
events.caveat: An alteration age cannot be assigned to magnetization without this link.
